root_cause.text: Race condition in DAMON where damos_walk() registers a new walk request under the walk_control_lock, but then checks the damon_ctx->kdamond pointer (protected by a different lock) to determine if the kdamond is still running; if the kdamond has already canceled all requests (under another lock) but hasn't yet cleared the kdamond pointer, damos_walk() sees the pointer as valid and waits indefinitely for a completion that will never occur.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description explicitly says "The damos_walk() requests registration and damon_ctx->kdamond unset are protected by different mutexes, though. Hence, damos_walk() could race with damon_ctx->kdamond unset, and result in deadlocks." The patch introduces walk_control_obsolete to synchronize termination state under walk_control_lock, preventing new requests after cancellation.

vuln_statements.explanation: Acquires the walk_control_lock to register the walk request, but does not protect the subsequent check of ctx->kdamond under the same lock, creating a race window.
Inserts the walk request into the list under walk_control_lock. If the kdamond has already canceled all requests under another lock, this request may be ignored and never completed.
Releases the walk_control_lock before checking ctx->kdamond, allowing a concurrent kdamond to cancel requests and clear the pointer without the walker seeing it.

Checks the kdamond pointer without holding the lock that protects it (likely kdamond_lock). If the kdamond has canceled all requests but not yet cleared the pointer, this condition evaluates true and leads to indefinite wait.
Waits for a completion that may never be signaled because the kdamond already canceled all pending requests (including this one) but the walker was not informed due to the race.
